statement.excerpt: This starts with a very simple statement: nobody has actually built a 1GW data center (to be clear, it’s usually a campus of multiple buildings networked together) yet.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: a campus of multiple buildings networked together
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that no single campus worldwide had at least 1,000 MW of commissioned, operational data-center capacity by publication.
The surrounding discussion makes completed shells, proposed capacity and partially commissioned projects insufficient.
I read the threshold as total facility power capacity. Critical IT power and instantaneous electricity consumption are different measures.

The observation concerns the publication-time state. I use May 1–12, 2026 as the current reporting interval, ending on publication; earlier snapshots provide context rather than direct evidence of that interval.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive, dated survey or equivalent operating records establishes that every plausible gigawatt campus remained below 1,000 MW of operational facility capacity at publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable dated records establish at least one single campus with 1,000 MW or more of commissioned, operational facility capacity by publication.
